title: Mapping the Intercalation-Induced Phase Transitions in LaTe3 via in situ Multimodal STEM
content: Studying phase transitions in situ is essential to understanding their evolution and, thus, engineering new or advanced technologies that exploit their potential [1]. This is especially true for battery materials where dramatic, intercalation-induced structural phase transitions affect safety, performance and reliability [2]. Among the available experimental probes, scanning transmission electron microscopy (S/TEM) is unique in its potential to provide simultaneous imaging, diffraction and spectroscopy data from a single instrument and at resolutions down to the atomic scale. In situ intercalation experiments in the TEM, however, are far from routine, often relying on highly specialized holders [3]. Here we utilize an off-the-shelf electronic chip (e-chip) placed in a standard Protochips Fusion350 heating/biasing holder to characterize, via a single experiment, the complete lithiation-induced phase transition in the layered van der Waals material, LaTe3. The geometry of our all solid-state electrochemical cell is shown in Fig. 1a and the basic LaTe3 structure is shown in Fig. 1c.
